structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E021.
1. Noise. Rebuilding the same commit only reshuffles results slightly: E017 and E019 (both dddcf96) read 0.7537 and 0.7541. Any change to kernels or graphs acts like a fresh 3-seed draw (E015–E017 share the same math and span 0.7537–0.7607). I put the per-seed SD at about 0.4 pp and the 3-seed SD at about 0.25 pp. My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.7555–0.756, so the real margin over 0.753 is only about 0.25 pp. E016's 0.7607 was a high draw. Filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes the filters, so the "wd gain" is mostly noise. If there is any real effect, it is in the BN-bias wd, and I expect it to be under 0.15 pp.
2. Epoch dial. E020 cut 1 true epoch (238→213 steps): −10.5% time and about −0.3 pp against the true mean. That is about 0.15 pp per 0.5 epoch, roughly 2.3 s per pp, still the best trade measured.
3. Architecture trades are worse than the dial. E021 narrowed group 2 to 320: −7.8% time (less than the 15% MAC cut, so time is not purely MAC-proportional; there are memory-bound elementwise and fixed costs), and −0.3 pp against the true mean, about 1.7 s per pp. E010's last group: −8.7% time and about −0.4 pp. On CIFAR-100, width is worth about as much per FLOP as epochs, or more. Group-1 depth is cheaper in MACs (about 7%), but the time saving will be smaller than the MAC share, and capacity at the first stage may matter for 100 classes.
4. Final-map regime (my mechanism). The 2x2 valid stem plus 3 pools gives a 3×3 final map at 28 and 32 px, but 2×2 at 20 and 24 px. Accuracy tracks the number of late steps in the 3×3 regime:
- E018 (28→24, 3×3→2×2) cost about 0.5 pp for 8.5% time.
- E011 cut both regimes and fell off a cliff.
- Under this mechanism, swapping 24→20 px early (2×2→2×2) should be nearly free in accuracy. But it only saves about 3–3.5% of time, since 15% of steps × (0.55−0.38) pixel weight is small.
Untested: 26 px (3×3 regime) in place of 28 px.
5. Time model. Time is about the sum of steps × pixel weight (23²/27²/31² for the stem output), plus about 0.3 s fixed, with sublinear savings from channel cuts.
6. Code facts: 3 Newton-Schulz steps; 238 true steps (9.5 epochs); BN momentum is effectively 0.4, so BN recalibration should be worth little; LR goes through a tensor fill (no recompile).
Unsure: E019's held-out 10-seed mean (not shown to me), the second point of the epoch slope, and judge-GPU transfer.
Best path: trim about 0.25–0.5 epoch while keeping the 3×3-regime step count. Stack it with a 20 px early phase and a 26 px middle phase. Accept only with a margin of at least 0.2 pp, given the noise.

forecasts.reason: Filter wd is inert and BN-bias wd is a weak lever. A gain of at least 0.2 pp over E016's lucky 0.7607 is very unlikely.
Time saving is sublinear in the ~7% of MACs removed, so it misses the 8% bar. Losing first-stage capacity costs about 0.3–0.5 pp.
20→24 px stays in the 2×2-final-map regime, so accuracy holds. But pixel arithmetic gives only ~3–3.5% time saving, just under the 4% bar.

cruxes: What was E019's held-out 10-seed mean and SD? If it is at or above 0.757, a 0.5-epoch trim (about −5% time) becomes affordable now.
Is the accuracy loss from the low-res phases set by the final-map regime (2×2 vs 3×3) rather than by pixel count? A 26 px middle phase (3×3 regime) losing at most 0.1 pp would confirm it.
Does the second point of the epoch slope (−0.5 true epoch on the tip) stay at or above 0.7545? That decides whether the epoch dial or the resolution levers should fund the next gains.
